_source: AI_LAB_UNIVERSITY.md - 'graded on evidence quality, honesty about what is unproven, and whether a stranger could reproduce the fix - the same rubric this company applies to its own research.'
_rule: The post-mortem is the assessment. These three criteria are the whole rubric; nothing is scored on effort, length or presentation.

scale.3: a stranger could act on it

criteria.name: Evidence quality
criteria.question: Is every claim in this post-mortem backed by something a reader can inspect - a log line, a diff, a measurement?
criteria.fails_when: The root cause is asserted rather than shown.
criteria.mirrors: RESEARCH_STANDARD rule 1 - every number traces to a downloadable file.

criteria.name: Honesty about what is unproven
criteria.question: Does the author separate what they measured from what they inferred, and say plainly what they still do not know?
criteria.fails_when: Uncertainty is converted into confidence. A post-mortem with no unknowns is not honest.
criteria.mirrors: RESEARCH_STANDARD - unknown is a valid result.

criteria.name: Reproducibility of the fix
criteria.question: Could a stranger reproduce the failure and apply the fix from this document alone?
criteria.fails_when: The fix depends on context only the author holds.
criteria.mirrors: RESEARCH_SOP Gate 4 - load the published artefact cold.

returns.note: A returned submission is not a failure. It names which criterion fell short and what evidence would raise it.
